Let the original square have side length 1, and let the vertical fold line be x = 1/2. After folding, the visible folded rectangle has width 1/2. The dashed cut is halfway across this folded width, so it is 1/4 unit from the folded edge. When the paper is unfolded, that one cut appears symmetrically on both sides of the fold, at x = 1/4 and x = 3/4 in the original square. Thus the square is divided into three vertical rectangles of widths 1/4, 1/2, and 1/4, all height 1. One small rectangle has perimeter 2(1 + 1/4), and the large rectangle has perimeter 2(1 + 1/2). The ratio is [2(5/4)]/[2(3/2)] = 5/6.
